views.reconstructed_statement: For every k,n in N and every L in R, assuming 0<L, put M=2^(n+1), p_j=-pi*L+j*(2*pi*L/M) for j in {0,...,M-1}, j_c=2^n, b_j=smoothInitial(k,p_j), and Z=sqrt(sum_{j=0}^{M-1} b_j^2). The root asserts the conjunction of these five statements: (1) p_{j_c}=0; (2) b_{j_c}=1; (3) sum_{j=0}^{M-1} b_j^2 >= 1; (4) Z>0; and (5) there exists a function a:Fin 2 -> R such that each a_j is strictly positive, a_0^2+a_1^2<1, and each a_j differs from 1. The existential function a in the fifth conjunct is independent of the displayed sampled family in the sense that the formula imposes no relation between a and b. Its existential quantifier is inside the quantifiers over k,n,L and the positivity hypothesis.

ambient_amplitude_definition: At a real coordinate p, smoothInitial(k,p) is exp(p) when p<-1; otherwise it is sourceInterpolant(k).eval(p) when p<=0; otherwise it is exp(-p). Consequently both p=-1 and p=0 use the middle polynomial branch.
Writing t=p+1, the supplied middle polynomial is exp(-1)*(1-t)^(k+1)*A_k(t)+t^(k+1)*A_k(1-t).
The supplied A_k(t) is sum_{r=0}^k [sum_{m=0}^r binom(k+r-m,k)/m!]*t^r. The two finite sums include both endpoints of their displayed natural ranges.
The root claims that the particular central sample at p=0 has value 1. It does not claim all samples have value 1.
sampleNorm(k,n+1,L) is defined as the nonnegative real square root of the same unweighted squared-sample sum appearing in the third conjunct.
claims_and_nonclaims: The conjunction asserts an exact central position, an exact central amplitude, a squared-mass lower bound of 1, and a strictly positive normalizer for the specified sampled family.
The root does not assert the squared mass equals 1, the normalizer equals 1, or any nontrivial upper bound on either.
No normalized vector b/Z is constructed in the root, although the strict positivity statement makes division by this Z meaningful.
The root contains no estimate of continuous interval mass, quadrature error, preparation success probability, circuit cost, or numerical conditioning ratio.
There is no biconditional or converse in this root; its first four conjuncts concern the supplied special family, and its last conjunct concerns a separately quantified function.
domains_and_boundaries: k and n range over all natural numbers including 0; the root has no k>=1 or n>=1 hypothesis.
L ranges over positive real numbers in the root. Statements outside this domain are not included in this root, even where individual supplied interfaces have a larger domain.
All sampled amplitudes, grid coordinates, sums, and square roots here are real. Squares are ordinary real squares, not complex amplitudes or complex absolute-value squares.
All sums over the sampled family are finite and unweighted: there is no grid-step factor, integral, average, or probability normalization in the mass expression.
existential_scope_and_separation: The literal scope is forall k,n,L,hL, (... and exists a, ...). A witness is formally allowed to depend on these outer parameters, but no parameter, sampledAmplitude expression, grid coordinate, or normalizer occurs in its defining conditions.
The existential does not assert that the sampled family b has squared mass less than 1; the sampled family has the opposite lower-bound claim in the third conjunct.
It does not assert that a is obtained by sampling smoothInitial, or that a agrees with b on any indices.
It asserts both entries of a are positive and neither is 1; it does not require a_0!=a_1 and does not specify numeric witness values.
The existential supplies an example with the listed properties. It is not a universal assertion about all strictly positive vectors.
length_and_index_conventions: The root passes N=n+1 to gridPoint, sampledAmplitude and sampleNorm. Thus the sample vector length is M=gridSize(n+1)=2^(n+1), not 2^n or n+1.
Its valid natural index values are 0,...,2^(n+1)-1. The finite index type is never empty and has at least two elements.
The supplied bit convention is j=sum_{i=0}^n bit_i*2^i. Thus bit_0 is least significant, and the central index 2^n has bit_n=1 and all lower bits zero.
For positive L, the uniform grid includes -pi*L at j=0 and excludes +pi*L at the upper end. Its spacing is 2*pi*L/2^(n+1).
centralIndex n is the valid Fin(2^(n+1)) index of natural value 2^n. The first conjunct says that coordinate is exactly 0.
At n=0 there are two sample positions, -pi*L and 0; the central index is 1. The existential a is still a separate Fin 2 function even in this equal-length case.
quantifier_order: For every k:N, then every n:N, then every L:R, then every proof hL of 0<L.

Under this positive-L hypothesis, assert the five conjuncts about the central grid point, central sampled value, squared-sample sum, square-root normalizer, and the existence of a separate two-entry real function.
Within the final conjunct there exists one a:Fin 2 -> R satisfying all three of: forall j, 0<a_j; the sum of both squared entries is <1; forall j, a_j!=1.
The same existential witness must satisfy all three properties. It is not a separately chosen witness for each property or each j.

views.reconstructed_statement: For every n in N and L in R, assuming 0<L, let h=2*pi*L/2^(n+1), c=Nat.ceil((-1+pi*L)/h), where Nat.ceil takes values in N and clamps negative inputs to zero, let S=search(n,0,-pi*L,pi*L), and let R=compute(n,L). The root asserts these five conjuncts: (1) R.value=c; (2) S.cost(field)=2*n; (3) S.cost(compare)=n+1; (4) R.cost(field)=2*n+2; and (5) R.cost(compare)=n+1. The costs are exact counts in the supplied charged exact-real operation model. They are not bit-operation, wall-clock, hardware-gate, or physical memory-access counts.

cost_model_semantics: Op consists of the distinct tags field, sqrt, angle, trig, compare, read, write, emit.
A Cost is a function from Op to N. tick(op) has value 1 at exactly op and 0 at the other tags.

charge(op,x) returns x and the corresponding one-operation cost. pure returns a value with all costs 0. bind adds componentwise the first cost and the cost of the subsequent computation selected by its value.
The field tag counts each declared real addition, subtraction, multiplication or division as one operation, without distinguishing their bit cost or implementing a finite-precision representation.
The compare tag counts calls to the exact real predicate below(x), which decides x<-1. It is not a count of all natural-number comparisons, proof obligations or physical branch instructions.
The appearances of the constant pi and of powers of two do not themselves cause trig, read, or other charges under the supplied definitions.
cutoff_and_length_conventions: h=gridStep(n,L)=2*pi*L/gridSize(n+1), with gridSize(n+1)=2^(n+1). The denominator is a positive real embedding of a natural power of two.
gridPointNat(n,L,j)=-pi*L+h*j for an unrestricted natural index j. This affine definition itself has no Fin-type restriction or modular indexing.
cutIndex(n,L)=Nat.ceil((-1-(-pi*L))/h). It is a natural number, so inputs of the ceiling at or below zero yield 0.

The supplied cutoff interface identifies the strict predicate gridPointNat(n,L,j)<-1 with j<cutIndex(n,L) for every natural j. Thus the cutoff is the first nonnegative index whose coordinate is at least -1, and a grid point exactly at -1 is not below the cutoff threshold.
The supplied interval interface bounds the cutoff by 2^n. The initial search interval runs from index 0 to index 2^n, namely from coordinate -pi*L to coordinate 0, with 2^n cells.

The coordinate 0 endpoint is included as a possible cutoff index even though the half-interval being partitioned has only the preceding 2^n cells. The full-grid length represented by the denominator is 2^(n+1).
If pi*L<=1, the clamped cutoff is 0. Otherwise the threshold lies to the right of the left endpoint. No assumption pi*L>1 appears in the root.
empty_and_boundary_cases: The relevant natural powers 2^n and 2^(n+1) are positive even at n=0; there is no empty-grid or zero-cell case in this root.
The positive-L hypothesis ensures h>0. The root does not cover L=0 or negative L.
The strict comparison is x<-1 throughout. Equality to -1 takes the false branch and belongs on the at-least--1 side of the cutoff.
cutIndex is natural rather than an arbitrary signed integer and may equal 0 or 2^n, so both search interval endpoints matter.
exact_claimed_cost_components: S.cost(field)=2*n and S.cost(compare)=n+1 refer to the standalone search with initial lower=-pi*L and span=pi*L; they exclude the two arithmetic operations that construct those inputs inside compute.
R.cost(field)=2*n+2 and R.cost(compare)=n+1 include those two compute preprocessing operations and the subsequent search.
All four are equalities of natural counters, not asymptotic bounds, timings, numerical error estimates, or probabilities.
The root explicitly projects only field and compare; it contains no quantifier over arbitrary op and no explicit equality for any of the other six components.

Separately, the supplied general cost interfaces state whole-vector formulas involving only tick(field) and tick(compare); within that declared model they would give 0 for the other tags. This is ambient interface information, not an additional root conjunct and not a claim of zero physical reads, writes, or memory usage.
instrumented_search_definition: At search depth r+1, a charged division computes half=span/2; a charged addition computes middle=lower+half; a charged exact comparison decides middle<-1.
If that comparison is true, the next state is search(r,start+2^r,middle,half); otherwise it is search(r,start,lower,half). Exactly one recursive branch is run.
At depth 0, a charged comparison decides lower<-1, and pure returns start+1 when true and start otherwise.
There are n recursive midpoint refinements in S and then one terminal comparison. Natural additions, index powers of two, branch control and counter bookkeeping are not charged in this model.
compute first computes width=pi*L with one charged field multiplication, then lower=0-width with one charged field subtraction, then runs search(n,0,lower,width).
quantifier_order: For every n:N, every L:R, and every proof hL of 0<L, assert the conjunction of the returned cutoff equality and four cost-component equalities.
No further input-validity, error-tolerance, bit-precision or resource-budget hypothesis appears.
The root includes n=0. At that depth the search has 0 charged field operations and 1 charged comparison, while compute has 2 charged field operations and 1 charged comparison.
The root is scoped to L>0; general cost interfaces in the packet quantify over a wider real domain, but that stronger quantifier is not part of this root.
value_claim_and_nonclaims: The only explicit value equality in the root is compute(n,L).value=cutIndex(n,L). The remaining conjuncts concern costs.
The root does not explicitly state the value of S in its standalone search expression, although the supplied compute definition and other interfaces explain its role.
The root does not return a sampled quantum state, construct an amplitude vector, output a circuit, or state a probability of success.

The exact-real ledger does not assert an implementation of exact real comparisons, finite-bit complexity, floating-point stability, precision requirements, total runtime, circuit depth, memory requirements, or hardware performance.
No numerical resource cost for natural index arithmetic, exponentiation of two, proofs, or counter maintenance is included. The names read, write and emit alone do not account for actual machine I/O.
No converse, optimality assertion, or lower bound for other algorithms is stated.
